name: Lesson 3 · Doing things: regular verbs in the present, the verb second

cards.note: Regular verbs: present-tense endings. ich: the stem wohn- (the infinitive minus -en) plus -e.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. du: the stem plus -st.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. er, sie and es: the stem plus -t.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. wir: the stem plus -en, the same as the infinitive. German has one present for both we learn and we are learning.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. ihr: the stem plus -t, the same ending as er.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. sie (they) takes -en, like wir.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. Formal Sie takes -en, like wir and they.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. ich: arbeit- plus -e.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. The stem ends in -t, so an extra e goes before -st to make it sayable: arbeitest.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. After a stem in -t, er takes -et: arbeitet. German uses the present for plans too.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. ihr also needs the extra e after the t: arbeitet.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. trink- plus -t. Kaffee has no article here, as in English.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. trink- plus -e.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. A noun subject takes the er ending: -t.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. die Katze is one subject, so trinkt, like sie.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. wir kaufen; the object der Tisch becomes einen Tisch.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. kauf- plus -t; sie with -t means she, not they.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. koch- plus -st.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. koch- plus -t. oft comes after the verb, not before it as in English.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. hören takes its object directly: no word for to.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. wir hören; oft follows the verb.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. German says I play gladly: gern after the verb means you like doing it.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. wir kochen + gern: we like to cook.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. The verb stays the main verb; gern only adds the liking.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. komm- plus -st.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. wir gehen: the -en form, the same as the infinitive.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. komm- plus -t.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. machen covers both make and do.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. lern- plus -t.
Regular verbs: present-tense endings. geh- plus -e.
The verb comes second. heute takes the first place, so the verb stays second and ich moves after it.
The verb comes second. Only one thing goes before the verb: morgen, then the verb, then wir.
The verb comes second. jetzt first, verb second, then the subject er.
The verb comes second. English keeps she before the verb; German puts the verb second and sie after it.
The verb comes second. A noun subject also moves behind the verb: kommt die Frau.
The verb comes second. hier can open the sentence too; then the verb comes second and wir follows.
The verb comes second. Any verb keeps the second place: heute, habe, ich.
The verb comes second. heute first, ist second, das Kind third.

cards.front: I am working today, but tomorrow I **have** time.
cards.back: Ich arbeite heute, aber morgen **habe** ich Zeit.
cards.note: The verb comes second. aber stands outside the count; morgen is first, so habe comes second.

cards.front: We play football often, and today we **are playing** too.
cards.back: Wir spielen oft Fußball, und heute **spielen** wir auch.
cards.note: The verb comes second. und does not count as a position: heute is first, spielen second.
